problem: Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$, find a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$
worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -5 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation $Ax=0$ is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{3}-7{x}_{4}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}-3{x}_{4}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution is ${x}_{1}=-4{x}_{3}+7{x}_{4}$ and ${x}_{2}=-{x}_{3}+3{x}_{4},$ where ${x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are free variables. Therefore, if $x\in \text{Null}(A),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{3}+7{x}_{4} \\ -{x}_{3}+3{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7{x}_{4} \\ 3{x}_{4} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3},{x}_{4}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

This implies that 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}
$$

is a basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\text{Null}(A).$
